# Critique — Pattern 15 (Immunological)

The slot allocation across the 255 slots was distributed as follows: Autoimmune Conditions (~20%), Allergic Conditions (~15%), Immunodeficiency & Chronic Infections (~15%), Vaccination History & Safety (~15%), Infection History (~15%), Inflammatory Markers, Autoimmune Treatments, & Family History (~15%), and self-monitoring fillers (~5%). Reaching the 255-question limit was straightforward due to the extensive list of autoimmune conditions and standard adult vaccines, though a few self-monitoring questions (positions 245–255) served as minor fillers. Overlaps exist with the Respiratory, Nutrition, and Metabolic domains (e.g., allergic asthma, celiac disease, type 1 diabetes) because immune mechanisms are the direct cause of these respiratory, digestive, and metabolic diagnoses. The V-flag was systematically set to `true` on questions representing vaccine adherence, biologic treatments, and wellness monitoring (e.g., up-to-date vaccines, HPV vaccine, regular screenings) to align with a convention where a stored bit `1` represents active disease, allergy, or immunodeficiency. We paraphrased guidelines from the AAAAI and vaccine schedules. The weakest question is position 253 ("Do you log your immunological symptoms weekly...") as weekly logging of immune symptoms is clinically arbitrary.
